lines: In the town of Wickmoor, it rained every night that autumn.
In the last house on Candle Lane, a girl named Mira was being told, for the fifth time, to go to sleep.
Mira had a cat called Nightpaw, because he walked around at night, and his paws were the night.
Every night, Mira sang the old rhyme.

Lose a penny, lose a key,
lose a ribbon off a tree —

all the things that slip from sight
tumble Underneath at night.

Hush now, hush, and hold on tight,
or Underneath will keep you. Quite.
Nightpaw did not like that rhyme. Cats know things.
Later, when the candle had burned down to a stub, something tapped at the window.
In the morning, the bed was empty.
The window was open. Small muddy footprints went over the sill and out into the garden...
...to the old well that Mira was never, ever allowed near.
Nightpaw had already spent eight of his lives, and had only one left.
